A \(4 \times 4\) block of calendar dates is shown. The order of the numbers in the second row is to be reversed. Then the order of the numbers in the fourth row is to be reversed. Finally, the numbers on each diagonal are to be added. What will be the positive difference between the two diagonal sums?

[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

Older television screens have an aspect ratio of \(4:3.\) That is, the ratio of the width to the height is \(4:3.\) The aspect ratio of many movies is not \(4:3,\) so they are sometimes shown on a television screen by “letterboxing” — darkening strips of equal height at the top and bottom of the screen, as shown. Suppose a movie has an aspect ratio of \(2:1\) and is shown on an older television screen with a \(27\)-inch diagonal. What is the height, in inches, of each darkened strip?

[Figure 1](attached-image-2)

Three cubes are each formed from the pattern shown. They are then stacked on a table one on top of another so that the \(13\) visible numbers have the greatest possible sum. What is that sum?

[Figure 1](attached-image-3)

A round table has radius \(4.\) Six rectangular place mats are placed on the table. Each place mat has width \(1\) and length \(x\) as shown. They are positioned so that each mat has two corners on the edge of the table, these two corners being endpoints of the same side of length \(x.\) Further, the mats are positioned so that the inner corners each touch an inner corner of an adjacent mat. What is \(x?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-4)

A \(4 \times 4\) block of calendar dates is shown. The order of the numbers in the second row is to be reversed. Then the order of the numbers in the fourth row is to be reversed. Finally, the numbers on each diagonal are to be added. What will be the positive difference between the two diagonal sums?

[Figure 1](attached-image-5)

On circle \(O,\) points \(C\) and \(D\) are on the same side of diameter \(\overline{AB},\) \(\angle AOC = 30^\circ,\) and \(\angle DOB = 45^\circ.\) What is the ratio of the area of the smaller sector \(COD\) to the area of the circle?

[Figure 1](attached-image-6)

In the figure, the outer equilateral triangle has area \(16,\) the inner equilateral triangle has area \(1,\) and the three trapezoids are congruent. What is the area of one of the trapezoids?

[Figure 1](attached-image-7)

In the figure, what is the ratio of the area of the shaded squares to the area of the unshaded squares?

[Figure 1](attached-image-8)

mappings.answerReason: The reversed rows are 11, 10, 9, 8 and 25, 24, 23, 22. The diagonal sums are 1+10+17+22=50 and 4+9+16+25=54, whose positive difference is 4.

mappings.rationale: The screen's aspect ratio and diagonal determine its dimensions through the Pythagorean theorem. The movie's aspect ratio then determines its height at the same width.
mappings.answerReason: Write the screen dimensions as 4k by 3k. Its diagonal is 5k=27, so its width is 21.6 and height is 16.2. The movie height is 21.6/2=10.8, giving each strip height (16.2-10.8)/2=2.7 inches.

mappings.rationale: Folding the net identifies opposite faces. Maximizing the exposed sum requires a bound on each cube's contribution and orientations that attain those bounds.
mappings.answerReason: The opposite pairs are (1,32), (2,16), and (4,8), and all six labels sum to 63. Each lower cube hides an opposite pair, so it exposes at most 63-12=51. The top cube hides one face and exposes at most 63-1=62. Putting 4 and 8 vertically on the lower cubes and 1 downward on the top cube attains 2×51+62=164.

routes.label: Solve the geometric quadratic by formula

mappings.rationale: The touching inner sides form a regular hexagon of side x and apothem √3x/2. Adding the mat width gives the distance to an outer chord. A right triangle with radius 4 produces a quadratic, which can be solved by either listed method.
mappings.answerReason: The radius to an outer corner gives 16=(x/2)²+(1+√3x/2)², so x²+√3x-15=0. Equivalently, (x+√3/2)²=63/4. The positive solution is x=(3√7-√3)/2.

mappings.rationale: After reversing the indicated rows, the task requires adding the four entries on each diagonal and subtracting the resulting two-digit sums.
mappings.answerReason: After reversal, the diagonals contain 1, 10, 17, 22 and 4, 9, 16, 25. Their sums are 50 and 54, so the positive difference is 4.

mappings.rationale: Subtract the two given central angles from the straight angle along the diameter, then use the sector's central-angle fraction of the whole circle.
mappings.answerReason: The smaller central angle COD is 180°-30°-45°=105°. Its sector therefore occupies 105/360=7/24 of the circle's area.

mappings.rationale: Subtracting the inner triangle's area leaves the three congruent trapezoids, which have equal areas. No triangle or trapezoid area formula is needed.
mappings.answerReason: The trapezoids together have area 16-1=15. Since they are congruent, each has area 15/3=5.

mappings.rationale: The central square has twice a small square's side length, so it has four times its area. Express both shaded and unshaded totals in small-square units and simplify their ratio.
mappings.answerReason: Taking each small square's area as 1, the central shaded square has area 4 and the two shaded corner squares contribute 2. The ten unshaded squares have total area 10, so the ratio is 6:10=3:5.
